clue.text: Skip the sauce

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playful leap or skip
second meaning: the pickled flower bud that goes into a classic sauce for mutton

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to leave out the sauce; in fact both halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a frisky jump, and caper sauce, made from pickled buds, is a traditional British accompaniment to boiled mutton.

clue.text: Age when Germans were kinder

parts.note: surface reading: an era when the German people behaved more gently
setter's reading: Kinder is German for children, so this is the age when a German was a child

explanation.walkthrough: The English word kinder hides the German Kinder, children.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of life when anyone is a child, German or otherwise, is the early stage before adolescence.

clue.text: Capital is at a discount

parts.note: par is face value, the benchmark against which a share is said to stand at a discount
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money is being offered cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, as at a discount suggests finance; it is the city. The parse is loose: par is only the reference point for a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: The French seat of government is a capital in the geographical sense of a country's chief city.

clue.text: Choicely entertained by King Edward

parts.note: regal means of or like a king
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone was treated to fine hospitality by King Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to feast them lavishly or amuse them with lively stories, entertaining them in style.

clue.text: Old-fashioned entertainment is back: there's a lot round everyone

indicators.note: round says the phrase for plenty wraps itself about the reversed pair of letters

parts.note: much means a great quantity

indicators.note: going back means the short word just before is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned about
all people together

explanation.surface: A grumble that a hackneyed old-time show has returned, with a crowd gathered round everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' could be the start of the wordplay, but it belongs to the definition of a vanished kind of British theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Music hall was the Victorian and Edwardian British variety theatre of comic songs and acts, now long out of fashion.

clue.text: It devoured children in an instant, with water

parts.note: a mo is a moment
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A monster gobbling up children in a moment, washed down with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Moloch was the Canaanite god to whom children were sacrificed by fire, and the name is now used for any devouring power.

clue.text: Office machine to add to the scrap-heap?

definitions.text: Office machine to add to the scrap-heap?

parts.note: surface reading: a piece of office equipment
setter's reading: the device turns paper into scraps, adding to the pile of waste

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'scrap-heap' is taken literally, a heap of paper scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The office device that cuts unwanted documents into thin strips for confidential disposal.

clue.text: Traffic light — always green

parts.note: surface reading: a set of signals at a road junction
setter's reading: a reflector set in the road, named after an animal's gleaming eye, which never turns red

explanation.walkthrough: Cat's-eyes are the glass reflectors set into British road surfaces; they light up in headlights but never switch to red.
explanation.definitionFit: A road stud that reflects headlights is a light for traffic, though it is not a signal and never changes.

clue.text: A day in November with a raw start and fog and packed snow to follow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of raw
mist is a thin fog
snow packed hard turns to ice

explanation.surface: A wintry November day that begins raw, with fog, and packed snow later.
explanation.walkthrough: Armistice Day, 11 November, marks the end of the First World War; the A of the clue does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Armistice Day is the anniversary on 11 November of the 1918 ceasefire, now kept as Remembrance Day.

clue.text: Left port with cargo

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Aden, the seaport in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship sailed out of harbour carrying its freight.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded, carrying a heavy burden, as a ship full of cargo is.

clue.text: An occasional boy for Holmes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: happening at uneven intervals, not regular
second meaning: one of the street urchins Sherlock Holmes hired as informants

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes now and then employs a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Conan Doyle stories the Baker Street Irregulars are a gang of street boys who gather information for Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular happens only now and then, and each of Holmes's street informants was called an Irregular.

clue.text: When retiring about to do this to the lamp?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: what you do to a lamp at bedtime: dim it

explanation.surface: A bedtime question: when going to bed, what should you do to the lamp?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like going to bed, which pairs with dimming the lamp; here it means shy. DIM IT read backwards gives TIMID.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person avoids company and attention, which is exactly what a shy, fearful or timid person does.

clue.text: A refugee — removed as Persephone was in Hades?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone forced from their homeland

definitions.text: removed as Persephone was in Hades
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Persephone was carried off from the world above to the underworld

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Hades abducted Persephone to the underworld, so she was literally a person taken out of her proper place.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaced person is the official term, used after the Second World War, for a refugee driven from their own country.

clue.text: Leg is legitimate in football

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the ...
second meaning: a player not offside is in a legal position

explanation.surface: A claim about which leg may legally be used in a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind the batsman's legs is called both leg and on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket names the leg half of the field the on side, and in football a player positioned legally is not offside.

clue.text: Working man, busier on the bed perhaps

indicators.note: working means being worked on and changed, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A labourer who works harder while lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' looks like a bedroom one; it is the sea bed, and the answer is the adjective meaning undersea.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means beneath the surface of the sea, as on the sea floor might be.

clue.text: Study of heredity in Indian Civil Service by leading French writer

indicators.note: the writer is leading, so his name goes in front of the other part

parts.note: Jean Genet, the French novelist and playwright
the initials of the Indian Civil Service

explanation.surface: A heredity study in the old Indian Civil Service, led by a prominent French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetics is the science of how traits are inherited, passed from parents to offspring through genes.

clue.text: Day for David to slice the Devil in two — good man!

indicators.note: slicing something in two lets another piece sit between the halves

parts.note: the first half of Satan, the Devil
St David's Day falls on 1 March, so March 1
the second half of Satan

explanation.surface: A man who cuts the Devil in half on a saint's day is a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: St David, patron saint of Wales, has his day on March 1, written in Roman numerals after the month's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable of the Good Samaritan, a Samaritan is anyone who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Red conspirator brought to court

parts.note: Cinna, one of the plotters against Julius Caesar
the bar is the court, as in being called to the bar

explanation.surface: A communist plotter is put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a communist; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a mercury ore whose bright scarlet colour gave its name to the pigment vermilion red.

clue.text: Careless of good French quality

parts.note: de bon is French for of good
an air is a manner or quality about a person

explanation.surface: Someone casual about the finer qualities of French things.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase de bon air, of good bearing, is where the English word comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person is carefree and nonchalant, carrying themselves with easy unconcern.

clue.text: They may be found in colonies, naturally

definitions.text: They may be found in colonies, naturally

parts.words: They may be found in colonies
parts.note: surface reading: creatures like ants or bees that live in groups
setter's reading: people who live au naturel, without clothes, in communal camps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonies' suggests insects or empire; it means camps of those who go without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists who go unclothed often gather in clubs or camps known as colonies.

clue.text: English hunts are backward in this respect

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for hunts from right to left

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of a hunt, so hunts are meets

explanation.surface: A remark that English fox hunts are behind the times in some regard.
explanation.walkthrough: A meet is the assembly of riders and hounds before a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration, the same thing as respect when used as a noun.

clue.text: Join together round one in private

indicators.note: round means going about, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to solder is to join metal pieces with melted alloy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: People uniting around one person in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective meaning secret; it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank in the army, an ordinary soldier.

clue.text: The Welsh were in fearful dread of the first

definitions.text: The Welsh were in fearful dread of the first

indicators.note: were in means placed inside the shaken word
fearful suggests shaken, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: The people of Wales were terrified of the first king of that name.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward I conquered Wales in the 1280s and ringed it with castles, so the whole clue is also a description of him.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward the First of England subdued the Welsh, who had good reason to fear him.

clue.text: Resist, then achieve rescue from robbers' demand

parts.note: to stand against is to resist
and then: one thing following another
to deliver someone is to rescue them

explanation.surface: Fight back, then manage to save yourself from the thieves' demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand and deliver was the classic order of the highwayman stopping a coach to rob its passengers.

clue.text: Fish was off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small silvery food fish

definitions.note: past tense: gave off a bad smell
definitions.meaning: second meaning: food that has gone off smells bad, in British past tense

explanation.walkthrough: Off means rotten in British use; the British past tense of smell is spelt with a t.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small sea or river fish, and food that was off would have stank, giving off an odour.

clue.text: Places of assignation out East for a beautiful woman

indicators.note: out tells us the following letter is removed from the word

parts.note: venues are meeting places
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Lovers' meeting spots that have gone abroad, in search of a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of VENUES is dropped to leave VENUS, the Roman goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus was the Roman goddess of love and beauty, and her name is used for any strikingly lovely woman.

clue.text: Prophet as follower of Samuel's teacher

indicators.note: being a follower means this little word comes after the other part

parts.note: Eli, the priest who brought up the boy Samuel in the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prophet described as a disciple of the man who taught Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet, used in the New Testament.

clue.text: Angela takes the Head for something to eat

parts.note: Angela Brazil, author of girls' boarding-school stories
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A girl named Angela goes to the headmistress to fetch a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Brazil was a popular early-twentieth-century British writer of schoolgirl stories, which fits the Head of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is the large edible seed of a South American tree, a familiar Christmas nut.

clue.text: Loved to out-stare — awfully rude

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the first word's letters are thrown about
awfully means badly done, so these letters too are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone liked nothing better than to stare others down, which is terribly impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasured means cherished, held very dear, which is to say deeply loved.

clue.text: Method of restraint incorporates second adhesive

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into one's body, so one part holds the other

parts.note: a rein holds back a horse
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A way of holding something back includes a second sticky substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky sap from trees, and synthetic resins are widely used as glues and binding agents.
